design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 02 editor top bar (« Aperçu du jeu ▷ » cluster). The « Exporter le jeu ⬇ » control sits in the right cluster before the disabled preview button. Low-fi, light theme; mono control like its siblings.

plan.goal: Export the authored book to a self-contained, versioned play-ready file (download) so a future play runtime can consume it without the editor.
acceptance_criteria: A « Exporter le jeu » control in the editor top bar downloads a JSON file named from the book title (slugified, .jeu.json).

The exported document is versioned (format 'genliv-play', version 1) and self-contained: book identity, all nodes (minus editor-only position), all edges INCLUDING the config-derived automatic edges (échec→Mort, KR-067), and the resolved acquirable-object catalog (collectObjects).

Export is a PURE transform over the BookService SSOT (no mutation, no private copy) and never blocks: dangling references (deleted targets/objects, unconfigured rules) are surfaced as structured warnings in the file and counted for the author, never silently dropped (KR-021).
After a successful export a transient status appears beside the button — « ✓ Export réussi » or « ⚠ N avertissement(s) » — and book:exported is emitted with the warning count.
The download helper revokes its object URL after triggering (no leak) and is a no-op outside a DOM; the status timer is ref-tracked and cleared on unmount.
The shared EditorTopBar stays feature-agnostic: book-export mounts via a generic actions slot, neither feature importing the other.
plan.walking_skeleton: A pure brain transform exportBookForPlay(book) builds the versioned play document (nodes minus position + authored edges + derived automatic edges + object catalog + dangling-reference warnings). A brain downloadJson util serialises + downloads it (Blob/objectURL/anchor, always revokes). The book-export feature's ExportGameButton (mounted into EditorTopBar's actions slot by the editor shell) reads the book from BookService, downloads the file, emits book:exported, and shows a transient success/warning status.

iterations.goal: Image upload (portrait/illustration), scenario import/export, AI prompt download
Warned-node highlighting after export: red NodeCard ring + OutlineView badge
Sommaire illustration: lightbox in ImageUpload, cover thumbnail in BookCard, full-bleed header in NodeScreen
Live structural validation: dead-end and dangling-edge-target always visible in canvas + outline during authoring, not only after export

known_risks: KR-119 — Play export is a PURE transform over the book SSOT (KR-020), baking the config-derived automatic edges (KR-067) + the resolved object catalog into one versioned, self-contained document; the download (Blob/objectURL/anchor) is a separate browser side-effect that ALWAYS revokes its object URL. Export is non-blocking: dangling references (KR-021) become file warnings + a count, never block or silently drop.

KR-120 — Shared editor chrome (EditorTopBar) stays feature-agnostic via a generic `actions` ReactNode slot the editor shell fills with feature buttons; the bar never imports a feature (Open/Closed; mirrors the SlotRegistry seam, KR-066/109).

KR-021 — References are by stable id; a target/object that no longer resolves must be surfaced, not silently broken — the export validates edge targets, prereq objects, countdown fallbacks, monster/PNJ targets, and décor object refs.
Timer-safety — the transient status timeout is ref-tracked and cleared on unmount + before re-scheduling.

KR-143 — importBook always mints a fresh book id (no collision); validates format marker + version + required fields + all node kinds before accepting. Returns null on any failure; callers guard the null.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton
architecture_choices: exportBookForPlay is a pure brain util (brain/utils/playExport.ts) over the book — it reuses deriveAutomaticEdges (fatal→Mort, KR-067) and collectObjects (catalog, KR-062) rather than recomputing, so the export can never disagree with the canvas/outline views. Nodes drop the editor-only `position` (KR-022/023); everything else is play data verbatim.

Referential-integrity report (KR-021): collectWarnings validates every by-id reference the domain carries — edge targets, hidden-prereq objects + countdown fallbacks (choice-linking), monster victoire/fuite + PNJ target/ref, and décor objectRef — returning structured { code, message, nodeId?, edgeId?, ref? } warnings. Non-blocking (user decision): the export always succeeds and reports the count.

Download is a separate browser side-effect util (brain/utils/download.ts): Blob + object URL + synthetic anchor click, the URL ALWAYS revoked in a finally (no leak), a no-op when there is no document. slugifyFilename derives a safe .jeu.json name from the title.

EditorTopBar gained a generic `actions` ReactNode slot (KR-120) filled by the editor shell with <ExportGameButton>; the bar never imports the feature. The button owns a transient post-export status (timer ref-tracked + cleared on unmount, timer-safety rule) and emits book:exported.
deviations_from_plan: New capability outside the ragged-iteration plan (like the choice-linking lineage refinement) — a single walking-skeleton slice (n=0), not part of a feature tier. Play mode itself stays deferred; this only produces the file it will consume.

iterations_log.label: warned-node highlighting
architecture_choices: ExportResult gains warningList: PlayWarning[] so callers can receive the full list, not just the count. The optional onResult prop on ExportGameButton is the seam: the editor shell (EditorScreen) passes a setter, keeping ExportGameButton self-contained.

warnedNodeIds derived via useMemo in EditorScreen (KR-013): nodeId-based warnings map directly; edgeId-based ones resolve to edge.from so the source node of the broken choice is highlighted, not an edge phantom.

Warning status no longer auto-hides: the timer only fires on a clean export (warnings === 0), so the ⚠ badge stays visible until re-export. Hovering it shows a native title tooltip with the message list.
NodeCard: warned prop → red border (--bad), red outer ring (--bad-line), red tinted background (--bad-bg). Selection takes priority (a warned+selected card still shows the accent).
OutlineView: OutlineRowItem gains warned bool → red text (--bad), tinted bg (--bad-bg), and an inline ⚠ span with aria-label='Référence cassée' for a11y.

test_coverage.unit: ExportGameButton: onResult receives [] on clean export; onResult receives [warning] on dirty export; warning status persists after dirty export. TreeCanvas: warned card carries var(--bad-line) ring after export. OutlineView: warned row shows aria-label=Référence cassée badge after export.
test_coverage.integration: full App: export triggers warnedNodeIds propagation to both views (canvas + outline tests)

iterations_log.label: sommaire illustration (cover + lightbox + player header)
architecture_choices: KR-055 exception: sommaire (structural but NOT locked) now accepts { text, illustration } patches in BookService.updateNode; mort still accepts { text } only. NodeEditorPanel gates the illustration section on node.kind !== 'mort' instead of !structural — the ImageUpload dropzone is visible for sommaire.

ImageUpload (brain/components) gains a lightbox: clicking the thumbnail opens a role=dialog fixed-overlay (position: fixed, inset: 0, z-index: 9999, semi-transparent). Click-outside and Escape both close it. useEffect subscribes to keydown only while the dialog is open.

BookCard (book-library) derives the cover URL inline: book.nodes.find(n => n.kind === 'sommaire')?.illustration. Renders as a full-width at the top of the card (object-fit: cover, height: 140px, borderRadius on top corners only). No brain event needed — BookCard already receives the live book prop.

NodeScreen (player) renders node.illustration as a full-bleed img before the padded text block: the img sits outside the padding container so it is edge-to-edge within the 680px max-width shell (maxHeight 360, object-fit: cover).

test_coverage.unit: ImageUpload: lightbox opens on thumbnail click; lightbox closes on backdrop click; lightbox closes on Escape key (4 new tests, 3 existing pass unchanged).
test_coverage.integration: book-library tests unaffected (no cover in seed books). NodeScreen behaviour unchanged (no illustration in seed nodes).

iterations_log.label: live structural validation (dead-end + dangling-edge-target)
architecture_choices: checkBookHealth(book): StructuralWarning[] in brain/utils/bookHealth.ts — pure function, no side effects, runs on every book change. Detects: dead-end (non-terminal, non-root node with no configured exit — stored edges OR monster.victoryTarget / pnj.target / trap.fatal) and dangling-edge-target (edge.to not found in nodeIds). Sommaire is exempt from dead-end (root always starts unconnected on a fresh book).

useBookHealth(bookId) in brain/hooks.ts wraps useOpenBook + useMemo; the same BOOK_MUTATION_EVENTS that trigger canvas/outline re-reads also trigger the health check. Exported from the brain barrel alongside StructuralWarning.

EditorScreen warnedNodeIds = union of live StructuralWarnings (always) + export PlayWarnings (after export). Live health uses StructuralWarning.nodeId directly (always set); export warnings still resolve edgeId → edge.from for edge-anchored issues. The two systems are complementary: live covers structural gaps; export covers deeper referential integrity (prereqs, countdowns, config targets).
KR-145: the sommaire root is exempt from dead-end detection because an unconnected root is the expected starting state of every new book; all other non-terminal nodes are checked immediately.
